paths.description: Public homepage and national forecast overview; represents global chrome, weather discovery and date-tab interaction.
Kanto/Tokyo forecast listing and Tokyo detail; represents the primary local-weather task.
Rain radar; represents the map-heavy interactive weather surface.
Earthquake index; represents urgent disaster-information listings.
Current forecaster article; represents editorial content, metadata and no-JavaScript delivery.
Address search for 東京 followed to a Tokyo forecast result; represents the main lookup journey.
Optional external authentication entry; inspected for labels, autocomplete and modern authentication.
Nonexistent route; represents HTTP error recovery.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture; computed styles report color-scheme: normal and a white body background under prefers-color-scheme: dark.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and retint surfaces, text, imagery chrome and form controls with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Interactive date/state changes are abrupt and do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rules while the homepage exposes eleven JavaScript date-state links that replace forecast state.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively wrap same-document forecast state changes in document.startViewTransition(), with a no-animation fallback and reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long pages provide static chrome rather than scroll-state guidance.
findings.evidence: The 7,062 CSS-pixel article and other long templates retain static top navigation; CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, progress indicator or scroll timeline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight reading/scroll progress cue or compact sticky header using scroll-state/container queries with a safe fallback.

findings.summary: Advertising and duplicated navigation substantially crowd the primary weather content.
findings.evidence: Desktop and article screenshots show background advertising, a right ad rail and dense repeated navigation around the weather/article content; the HAR records extensive ad-tech delivery.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve the first viewport for forecast/article content, collapse duplicate navigation, and defer nonessential ad/recommendation modules until near viewport.

findings.summary: Public pages ship a fixed desktop layout to phones, making core weather tasks tiny and difficult to operate.
findings.evidence: Every tested 360x800 page lacked a viewport meta tag and rendered a 1088–1248 CSS-pixel desktop canvas scaled to 0.29–0.33. Text and controls are miniature across homepage, forecast, radar, earthquake, article and search.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a scalable width=device-width viewport and rebuild the shared shell/content grids mobile-first with fluid intrinsic sizing, reflowing columns and adequately sized controls; do not disable zoom.

findings.summary: The homepage misses fast-load and interaction performance targets.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.64s, TBT 770ms, Speed Index 16.1s and performance 0.47; the independent trace measured LCP 12.50s and four long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the forecast LCP, delay ads/analytics until after critical content, break up long tasks and validate LCP/INP/CLS under representative mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Third-party and unused code dominate resource delivery.
findings.evidence: HAR: 356 requests and 4.90 MB transferred, including 72 scripts/2.71 MB and 343 third-party requests. Lighthouse estimates 1,562 KiB unused JavaScript and reports render-blocking savings of 2,980ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant vendors, conditionally load nonessential scripts, defer/async confirmed noncritical scripts, shorten dependency chains and set useful cache lifetimes.

findings.summary: Interactive and image content lacks accessible names.
findings.evidence: axe found critical image-alt failures on three images, one unnamed member link, and Lighthouse found an unnamed button; the address input has no programmatic label.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide meaningful alt text or decorative semantics, label the address field, and give every link/button a stable accessible name.

findings.summary: Text and links fail minimum contrast requirements.
findings.evidence: axe reports 44 serious colour-contrast failures and links distinguishable only by colour in text blocks.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to WCAG AA and add a non-colour affordance such as underline for inline links.

findings.summary: Landmarks, headings and focus order are structurally inconsistent.
findings.evidence: axe found no main landmark, 63 regions outside landmarks, duplicate navigation landmarks, skipped heading order and tabindex=2. The DOM contains an H1 followed by H3 sections.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in main, uniquely label navigation landmarks, use sequential headings, and remove positive tabindex values while preserving visible focus.

findings.summary: The page logs runtime errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse errors-in-console audit failed during a clean homepage load.
findings.suggestedFix: Reproduce the logged errors in DevTools, fix first-party exceptions and isolate or remove failing third-party integrations.

findings.summary: Document assets are incompletely sized and inefficiently encoded.
findings.evidence: The images audit found 9 images without dimensions, 10 oversized images and 60 of 66 in legacy formats; doctype and UTF-8 charset were valid.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, generate right-sized responsive sources and prefer AVIF/WebP where appropriate.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and DevTools inspector issues remain in production.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports two deprecated-API warnings and a failed inspector-issues audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API usage, resolve Chrome Issues-panel diagnostics and retest BFCache/source-map hygiene.

findings.summary: Mobile and crawler navigation signals contain avoidable defects.
findings.evidence: The page has no viewport meta tag and 17 javascript: links; Lighthouse fails crawlable anchors and mobile viewport audits. robots.txt itself is reachable and advertises two sitemap URLs.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href URLs for forecast states with click enhancement, add a user-scalable responsive viewport, and preserve descriptive link text.

findings.summary: Security policy and cookie defaults are too weak.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff and frame protection are present, but CSP is absent. Cookie inspection found 17 cookies without Secure and many SameSite=None/long-lived analytics identifiers.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure; use Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is essential and shorten analytics retention.

findings.summary: The default page load has an excessive tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 70 third-party origins and 26 known tracker domains. HAR attributes 343/356 requests and 4.86/4.90 MB to non-main origins, including DoubleClick, Taboola, Meta, TikTok and Clarity.
findings.suggestedFix: Establish a strict vendor allowlist, load optional analytics/ads only after meaningful consent or interaction, minimise identifiers and batch necessary telemetry.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only and misses complete autofill semantics.
findings.evidence: The login page exposes email and password fields, no passkey/WebAuthn affordance, and the email field has an empty autocomplete token; the OAuth request does use PKCE.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey/WebAuthn sign-in and registration, retain password recovery as fallback, and set username/email plus current-password autocomplete tokens.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policy coverage is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Permissions-Policy is missing and HSTS max-age is only 300 seconds; Referrer-Policy and X-Frame-Options are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, lengthen HSTS after rollout confidence, and express frame-ancestors in CSP.

findings.summary: Search and login inputs do not provide complete autocomplete assistance.
findings.evidence: The address/postcode search input has no autocomplete token or label; the login email field also has empty autocomplete while only the password has current-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Label the search field and add appropriate postal-code/street-address semantics; use username or email and current-password tokens on login.

findings.summary: Images are not consistently optimised for transfer or display size.
findings.evidence: Images audit: 60/66 legacy-format images, 18 without srcset, 10 oversized and 32 below-fold images not lazy-loaded; one decorative banner transfers 876 KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive sources, choose correct display sizes, lazy-load below-fold media and remove or recompress the 876 KB decorative banner.

findings.summary: Background ad and analytics work is disproportionate to the weather task.
findings.evidence: A single load triggers 134 XHR/fetch requests and 70 third-party origins; Lighthouse records 9.5s main-thread work and 7.0s JavaScript execution.
findings.suggestedFix: Stop background vendor work when not visible, conditionally load integrations, coalesce telemetry and prioritise only user-visible weather requests.

findings.summary: The third-party and media budget is not proportionate.
findings.evidence: Third-party delivery accounts for 4.86 MB and 343 requests; large ad/recommendation scripts and decorative images surround a comparatively lightweight forecast document.
findings.suggestedFix: Set enforceable per-template budgets for third-party requests/bytes and delay or remove vendors and media that do not improve the primary task.

findings.summary: The homepage has a disproportionately large initial memory footprint.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary contains 1,456,317 nodes and 73.7 MB self size, including 161,933 closures. After date-tab repetition it reaches 76.7 MB, although DOM count remained stable and this pair did not prove an unbounded leak.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce vendor scripts and closure-heavy integrations, lazy-initialise below-fold modules and enforce a retained-heap budget in repeated-interaction tests.

Repair names, landmarks, headings and colour contrast

Optimise and correctly size image delivery
Make navigation state crawlable and add valid viewport metadata
Resolve runtime errors, deprecated APIs and inspector issues
Add passkeys and complete input/autofill semantics
Respect dark mode and progressively enhance state motion
Reduce ad chrome around primary content
